We're not globohome. Freemasonry is not one massive organisation, but rather a collection of grand lodges.

Each country (or state in the US) has their own grand lodge. Sovereignty is extremely important. Each grand lodge has their own version of the base core rules of freemasonry.

For example, some grand lodges in the US don't allow gay people, some grand lodges in Scandinavia are focused on Christians, etc.

If a grand lodge changes the rules too much (ie. allow women for example), other grand lodges will stop recognizing that grand lodge).

As long as you satisfy the requirements, you can become a member. These are 18 years old, male, belief in a Supreme Being and no criminal record (no felonies). You don't need to know any masons to get in.

Every state in Australia has their own grand lodge. Just check http://www.masonicsourcebook.com/freemasonry_directory_grand_lodges_Australia.htm for a link to the grand lodge of your state. These websites should either have a contact form or a list of lodges which you can then contact.

You would become part of the largest and oldest fraternity on earth. You would gain brothers. You will learn and more importantly experience masonic symbolism.

Even though we keep things secret, you can find everything online. Only problem is that as a non-mason, you don't know what's true, what means what exactly, etc. But the experience cannot be found online.

I stay because of the brotherhood. I joined for the symbolism and I still learn more every day and feel that it has had a great effect on my life. However, the brotherhood is amazing. Meeting someone from the other side of the world and it feels like you're meeting your life-long brother.

There are dues, but they are not proportional to your income. Mine are 246 euros per year (but they vary from area to area). These are used for building upkeep and whatnot. Every master mason of a lodge can see the finances, so you know exactly where the money is going.

Anonymous ID:7r6P46Hb Sat 24 Aug 2019 12:10:32 No. 224214148 Report
Quoted By: >>224214714
>>224213944

Freemasonry for dummies focusses on what freemasonry is, the fraternity, etc.

The initiatic experience focusses on the importance of initiation in human civilisation

Bible study for freemasons highlight the relevant biblical verses. The author wrote it such that non-masons can also read it. You won't have the context within freemasonry, but you can have the biblical inspiration.

The secret science of masonic initiation has a sensational title, but it's an interesting discussion of the initiation.

Freemasonry and the birth of modern science show how important freemasonry was to the development of the royal society.

Contemplative masonry is more about how to apply freemasonry in real life. It won't make too much sense as a non-mason, but still an interesting read.
